articles.title: ‘Mosquito Bowl’: Football Stars on the Front Lines
articles.summary: Peter Berg’s ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ is essentially ‘Friday Night Lights’ meets ‘Hacksaw Ridge.’
articles.summary_zh: Peter Berg's The Mosquito Bowl本质上是周五夜灯, 这部电影具有与星期五夜光相同的创意氛围(gritty手持相机、哑调色板、天空后摇滚声道的爆炸), 也像伯格的星期五夜光一样, 《蚊子碗》(现在在剧院里; 2022年的一本书——副标题是《二战中的生死游戏》——只有一章(41篇)专门讲述1944年的足球比赛,被誉为“蚊子碗”。 书中大部分内容是关于战争的,而留下妻子,孩子的年轻人,以及有前途的NFL职业来对抗战争.
articles.title_zh: “蚊子碗” ：前线的足球明星
articles.content: Peter Berg’s The Mosquito Bowl is essentially Friday Night Lights meets Hacksaw Ridge . It’s a movie with the same creative vibe as Friday Night Lights (gritty handheld camera, muted color palette, Explosions in the Sky post-rock soundtrack) but applied to a brutally violent true story of WWII’s Battle of Okinawa, one of the single bloodiest battles of the 20th century. Also like Berg’s Friday Night Lights , The Mosquito Bowl ( out now in theaters ; coming to Netflix November 25) is based on a book by Pulitzer Prize–winning journalist Buzz Bissinger . The 2022 book—subtitled A Game of Life and Death in World War II —only has one chapter (of 41) devoted to the actual 1944 football game dubbed “The Mosquito Bowl.” Most of the book is about the war, and the young men who left wives, kids, and promising NFL careers to fight it. Likewise, Berg’s film adaptation is mostly a somber, unflinching WWII film, with a brief reprieve of joy in the form of a football game on Guadalcanal between the 4th and 29th regiments of the 6th Marine Division. Just as in Friday Night Lights , where the drama of high school football parallels the struggles and triumphs of life off the field, the football game in The Mosquito Bowl parallels the “game of life and death” that surrounds the men at war. Sports are interesting in this way: They provide escape from real life but also training for it, an arena of danger and high stakes but not ultimate stakes. Sports often map onto life—we draw up plans and plays but have to improvise; we get hurt but can heal; we thrive individually through teamwork; sometimes we win and sometimes we lose. Yet sports are unlike real life too. Winning or losing on the field is a matter of trophies and glory, but off the field, it can be a matter of life and death. Young Men Willing to Fight and Die The Mosquito Bowl (rated R for graphic war violence and language), opens with a well-known epigraph from Herbert Hoover : Older men declare war. But it is youth that must fight and die. And it is youth who must inherit the tribulation, the sorrow, and the triumphs that are the aftermath of war. This is a movie about youth—or rather, the passage from youth into adulthood that war accelerates. This is a movie about youth—or rather, the passage from youth into adulthood that war accelerates. The movie opens with muddy college football scenes in the fall of 1941, as the four central characters are introduced: John McLaughry (Nicholas Galitzine), Brown quarterback; Bob Baumann (Bill Skarsgård), University of Wisconsin tackle; Tony Butkovich (Ray Nicholson), Purdue fullback; and Dave Schreiner (Tom Francis), Wisconsin end. They were all-star athletes with promising futures. Many of them were collegiate All-Americans and drafted by NFL teams. Yet December 7, 1941, happened, and their futures were all changed. Once bound together by football skill, friendly rivalry, and fierce competition on the gridiron, these men soon bonded in a different setting: as marines in WWII’s savage Pacific theater. Instead of fighting for yards on the field, they fought for ground in a war of attrition on Okinawa. Instead of a football in hand, they carried guns and bayonets. Instead of tackling their opponents, they wrestled them to the death in hand-to-hand combat. Like many in the Greatest Generation, these men volunteered to enlist and fight. The Mosquito Bowl celebrates their duty and sacrifice. In one scene, Baumann’s younger brother says, “You don’t have to go,” to which Baumann replies, “I do. I’m needed.” It’s hard to imagine star athletes, whether collegiate or professional, volunteering to go to war in 2026. But in 1943, it was normal. Okinawa, Bissinger writes in the book, was “by far the largest collection of athletes ever to die in a single battle.” And in the entirety of WWII, 21 NFL players died in combat, as well as two players from Major League Baseball. Why were they so willing to lay down their lives? Perhaps back then, men had the bigger horizon more in view. Life isn’t about serving oneself. It’s about serving others, fighting for things bigger than personal fulfillment. As Dave Schreiner tells John McLaughry, “This is us sacrificing for the unborn. What other real thing is there? What’s the point in all of this if it’s not for passing something on?” Numbed by War-Movie Violence The Mosquito Bowl honors the Greatest Generation and is commendable in its straightforward embrace of manly virtues like duty and sacrifice. But I disliked several aspects of the film. One is the language. I realize wartime soldiers in every era tend to be prolific in their employment of profane language. But even if men in the 1940s were as creative with the f-word as they are in this movie, is it really essential to the movie? It makes the film much less likely to be watched by families, which is a shame because it’s the sort of thing dads might want to watch with their younger sons. I also wish Berg had given less screen time to bloody battles and more time to quieter character moments and the titular football game. I get that it’s important to underscore the savage bloodbath that was the Pacific theater, and I get that the joyful escape of football is most pronounced when juxtaposed with the horrific realities of war. But it’s hard for contemporary war movies to viscerally depict the “war is hell” experience after the genre has been so saturated. Edward Berger’s adaptation of All Quiet on the Western Front (2022) felt like the final word on war-movie blood and guts. We’ve become numb to watching bodies get mangled every which way. Going forward, movies about savage warfare probably need to take a different approach. There are ways to capture battle horror without showing every gruesome detail. Furthermore, the desaturated, shaky-camera, chaotic choreography of war movies has become clichéd. I checked out a bit during these prolonged battle scenes. At times, it felt like Berg was inspired by Terrence Malick’s Guadalcanal movie, The Thin Red Line (one of the best war movies of all time). But what made Malick’s film so effective is that it employed violence only in a few intense, lyrical sequences, juxtaposed with long stretches of more contemplative material and tender character moments. The experience of war is important to capture accurately. But a war film becomes great when the meaning of war is also a focal point. Clint Eastwood’s WWII diptych, Flags of our Fathers and Letters from Iwo Jima (2006), strikes this balance well. The action-to-reflection ratio is not quite right in The Mosquito Bowl . Football as Far as the Curse Is Found The high point of Berg’s movie is the Mosquito Bowl game, even though it occupies too little of the overall runtime. In a movie that is rather bleak thematically and visually, the game provides a much-needed moment of joy for the characters and audience. Hosted as a morale booster for soldiers who would soon be sent to fight on Okinawa, the game (broadcast on the “mosquito radio network”) was set up to be “two-hand touch” only but quickly devolved into full-on tackle. Some of the guys wore Santa hats. There were big smiles, laughs, playful rivalry: young men allowed to be boys again. Here’s how Bissinger describes it in the prologue of his book: For roughly two hours the Mosquito Bowl wasn’t simply a reminder of what life had once been like for the players, but freedom and abandon, with the spectators captured in the same moment, screaming their heads off, whether drunk or sober. The beauty of sports, the ultimate power of it to carry you away, had never been stronger. But the scene is also bittersweet, for we know it’s not reality. Real life is harsh. Okinawa looms. Many of these boys playing football on Christmas Eve 1944 won’t live to see Christmas Eve 1945. This scene reminded me of the resonant poetry of Friday Night Lights , which depicted football in much the same way: youthful vibrancy and freewheeling joy, but tempered by the painful pressures

Peter Berg's The Mosquito Bowl本质上是周五夜灯, 这部电影具有与星期五夜光相同的创意氛围(gritty手持相机、哑调色板、天空后摇滚声道的爆炸),
也像伯格的星期五夜光一样, 《蚊子碗》(现在在剧院里;
2022年的一本书——副标题是《二战中的生死游戏》——只有一章(41篇)专门讲述1944年的足球比赛,被誉为“蚊子碗”。 书中大部分内容是关于战争的,而留下妻子,孩子的年轻人,以及有前途的NFL职业来对抗战争.
同样,伯格的电影改编作品大多是一部默默无闻的WWII电影,以第6海军陆战队第4团和第29团在瓜达尔卡纳尔(Guadalcanal)的足球比赛形式短暂地延缓了欢乐.
就像星期五夜光节一样,高中足球的戏剧与场外生活的斗争和胜利平行,蚊子碗的足球比赛与围攻战中男子的“生死游戏”平行。 体育就是这样有趣的: 它们提供了脱离现实生活的机会,但也为它提供了培训,这是一个危险和利害攸关的场所,但不是最终利害攸关。
体育往往描绘在生活中——我们制定计划和玩耍,但必须即兴发挥;我们受到伤害,但能够治愈;我们通过团队合作单独繁荣;有时我们赢,有时我们输。 但体育也不像现实生活 胜败于田,是功勋之事,但从田,可以生死之事.
这是一部关于青年的电影, 这是一部关于青年的电影, 电影在1941年秋天以泥巴的大学足球场景开场,因为四个中心人物被介绍:约翰·麦克劳格利(英语:John McLaughry (Nicholas Galitzine)),布朗四分卫;
鲍勃·鲍曼(英语:Bill Skarsgård),威斯康星大学攻克;托尼·布特科维奇(英语:Ray Nicholson),普尔杜(英语:Purdue fullback)和戴夫·施雷纳(英语:Dave Schreiner)(Tom Francis),威斯康星州结束. 他们是全明星运动员 前途光明 其中许多人都是全美联军,由NFL球队起草. 然而,1941年12月7日却发生了,他们的未来都发生了变化.
这些人曾经被足球技巧、友好竞争和激烈的竞争捆绑在一起,他们很快就在不同的环境下被束缚在一起:作为海军陆战队员在二战期间的野蛮太平洋剧场里。 在冲绳的一次自然减员战争中,他们没有在战场上争夺码数,而是争夺地面. 他们没有手持足球,而是携带枪支和刺刀.
他们与其对付对手,不如在手牵手的战斗中将他们摔死. 和"最伟大的一代"中的许多人一样,这些人自愿入伍和参战. 蚊子碗庆祝他们的职责和牺牲. 在一个场景中,鲍曼的弟弟说:"你不必去,"鲍曼回答说:"我愿意.
需要我。 很难想象明星运动员, 但是在1943年,这是正常的. Bissinger在书中写道, 冲绳是“迄今为止在一次战斗中死亡的运动员人数最多的集合”。 而在整个二战中,21名NFL球员在战斗中丧生,还有来自主力联赛棒球的两名球员.
为什么他们这么愿意牺牲自己的生命? 也许那时 男人的视野更大了 生活不是为自己服务。 而是为他人服务, 正如Dave Schreiner对John McLaughry所说,“这是我们为未出生的人而牺牲。 还有什么东西?
如果不是为了传递东西, 《蚊子碗》以战争电影暴力为蓝本 向最伟大的一代致敬 并值得称赞的是 它直截了当地拥抱了 诸如责任和牺牲之类的人性美德 但我不喜欢电影的几个方面。 一是语言.
我知道每个时代的战时士兵在使用淫秽语言方面往往很繁琐. 但是,即使20世纪40年代的男子与本片中的f-word一样具有创意,这是否真的对电影至关重要? 影片更难被家人观看,
我也希望伯格给 较少的屏幕时间 对于血腥的战斗, 更多的时间 安静的角色时刻 和三角足球比赛。 我理解强调太平洋剧场的野蛮流血很重要,
但当代战争电影很难直面“战争就是地狱”, Edward Berger)改编的"西部战线上的全静"(2022年),感觉就像关于战争-电影的血和胆的最后一句话. 我们已麻木,
展望未来,关于野蛮战争的电影可能需要采取不同的做法。 有一些方法捕捉战斗恐怖而不展示每一个可怕的细节. 此外,战争电影的不饱和、摇摇欲坠、杂乱无章的配乐也成了陈词滥调。 在漫长的战斗场景中 我查了一下
贝格有时觉得受到特伦斯·马利克的瓜达尔卡纳尔电影"瘦红线"(The Thin Red Line)的启发(这是有史以来最好的战争电影之一). 但马利克的影片之所以如此有效, 是因为影片只使用几段激烈的、充满诗歌的情节,
战争的经验对于准确捕捉是重要的. 但当战争的意义也是焦点时,战争电影就变得伟大. Clint Eastwood的二战Diptych, 我们父亲的旗帜和来自硫磺岛的信件(2006年), 《蚊子碗》中的动作与反射比率并不完全正确。
足球如魔咒的发现 Berg电影的高潮是蚊子碗游戏, 在一部相当暗淡的主题和视觉电影中,游戏为角色和观众提供了非常需要的欢乐时刻.
游戏(在“Mosquito电台网络”上播出)仅是“两手触摸”, 有些家伙戴圣诞老人帽 曾出现大笑,大笑,玩耍的对战:青年男子允许再次成为男孩.
Bissinger在他的书前言中, 蚊子碗在大约两个小时的时间里, 体育的美丽, 它的终极力量 把你带走,从来没有更强大。
但场面也很苦涩, 现实生活很残酷 冲绳开始出现。 许多人在1944年平安夜踢足球, 这个场景让我想起周五夜光的反响,

articles.title: Pastor, Be Opportunistic
articles.summary: Pastor, you cannot afford to coast. You cannot afford autopilot. Be a gospel entrepreneur. Eternity is at stake.
articles.summary_zh: 我的咖啡凉了,因为教堂规划师 哀悼他的教堂感到停滞。 更糟糕的是,一种浓郁的怨恨已经笼罩在众会的身上。 前三年令人兴奋; 社区被一个新的教会工厂所吸引, 真正好奇的是它是什么。
articles.title_zh: 牧师，抓住机会
articles.content: My coffee had gone cold as the church planter mourned that his church felt stagnant. Worse than not growing—a thick malaise had settled over the congregation. The first three years were exciting; the community was intrigued by a new church plant, genuinely curious about what it was all about. But everything had plateaued. Leaders grew complacent. Sundays—even with strong preaching—felt cold and passionless. The church’s reason for existing had shrunk to feeding and caring for the Christians who already called it home. The church planter couldn’t see how it was still transforming the community. An older mentor at the table cleared his throat. “I’m sorry to hear that. Let me ask you—what is one risky, hard thing the Lord is inviting your church to do that you’re hesitant to do?” The planter scratched his head. “I don’t know. I’ve never been asked that before.” The older man shrugged. “Every pastor should be ready to answer that question. If he can’t, he needs to spend some time praying and fasting until he can. Comfort and complacency are incredibly dangerous.” I’ve sat in enough of these conversations to know that wise, healthy risks are vital to the life of the church. Without them, the church atrophies. Its reason for existing collapses into self-care and, after a few years, into self-preservation. Risky and hard things keep gospel blood flowing through the body. Pastor, you cannot afford to coast. You cannot afford autopilot. You owe it to Jesus and to your church to make the most of opportunities in your city—which means that alongside preaching, teaching, praying, and developing leaders, you need to prioritize seeking new avenues for ministry. Be a gospel entrepreneur. Church-planting networks have long understood that entrepreneurial aptitude is essential for planters. But what about established churches—do their pastors need to be entrepreneurial too? What Is a Gospel Entrepreneur? There’s still hesitancy around saying pastors need entrepreneurial aptitude. Maybe it’s because we picture someone who constantly starts new things he can’t sustain—a person with a billion ideas who follows through on none of them. If this is what we mean, then no, we don’t want our pastors to be entrepreneurial. Comfort and complacency are incredibly dangerous. But a gospel entrepreneur is something different. He doesn’t pile up harebrained ideas. He stays awake and sober-minded about the opportunities the Lord is opening in the community. He sees the wooden frames of a new development and prays about how the gospel will reach those families once they move in. He looks at neighborhoods where existing churches can’t possibly reach everyone—and plants a church there. He saves, scrimps, and sacrifices to move a growing church plant into a more strategic location. He keeps his eyes open, his mind sharp, and his hands ready for the moment God opens a door. Biblical Call When this topic comes up, someone usually asks, “Where do you see the need for a pastor to be an entrepreneur in the Bible?” My answer often surprises people: Jesus’s parable of the dishonest manager. In Luke 16:1–9, a rich man discovers his property manager has been wasting his possessions and tells him to settle accounts—he’s about to be fired. The manager realizes losing his job means either digging or begging, so he immediately goes to work cutting deals to gain favor with other wealthy employers. When his employer finds out, he commends the manager for his shrewdness. Ethical or not, it was a genius move. At this point, we should ask, Why is Jesus telling this story? Maybe he’s about to indict people like the manager. But the manager’s dishonesty has nothing to do with Jesus’s point. The twist is that Jesus holds up the dishonest manager as an example of what he wants his disciples to be. “The master commended the dishonest manager for his shrewdness,” Jesus says. “For the sons of this world are more shrewd in dealing with their own generation than the sons of light” (Luke 16:8). The parable is, if anything, a lament. The world’s sons do a better job seizing opportunities to advance their kingdoms than we do in advancing Christ’s. The implication is sobering. The sons of light need to be as intentional and opportunistic about eternity as the world is about temporary gain. We need pastors who will prayerfully take risks, do hard things, feel the urgency, and grab opportunities. A gospel entrepreneur stays awake and sober-minded about the opportunities the Lord is opening in the community. Consider it this way. Walmart and Target already have plans for that empty lot next to the new development. Millions of dollars are being spent on demographic studies and marketing campaigns to grow somebody’s bottom line. Believe it or not, there’s probably a developer with more aggressive ideas for your church building than you have. I’ve even heard a story of a dying church in a small Colorado town that was slowly pushed out of its building—a local developer sent people to join as members, just so they could vote to sell. The sons of the world know how to expand their kingdoms. In the verses that follow the parable, Jesus connects the parable to faithfulness in little things, stewarding earthly resources well, and remembering that we serve God, not our budgets and assets. Our goal as pastors isn’t to keep our congregants happy, live off endowments, or maintain the institution’s favorite donors. Our job is to call people to pick up their crosses and follow Jesus into risky opportunities, where even if we die, people will see Jesus. Don’t Be Risk Averse The dishonest manager knew he had no time to be risk-averse or complacent. He had to seize every opportunity to save his own skin. Pastors and churches have no time to be risk-averse either—not for our own sake but for the gospel’s. Eternity is at stake. Pastor, be a gospel entrepreneur. When we stand before our Lord on the last day, may it not be true that the sons of the world had a greater influence on our community than we did.
articles.content_zh:
我的咖啡凉了,因为教堂规划师 哀悼他的教堂感到停滞。 更糟糕的是,一种浓郁的怨恨已经笼罩在众会的身上。 前三年令人兴奋; 社区被一个新的教会工厂所吸引, 真正好奇的是它是什么。 但一切都已经稳定下来了。 领导人越来越自满。
星期天,即使有强烈的传教,也感到冷酷无情。 教堂的存在原因已经缩小,只能供养和照顾已经称之为家的基督徒。 教会的植树造林者看不出它如何仍在改变社区。 餐桌上一位年长的导师清了喉咙. 我很遗憾,
我问你,上帝邀请你的教会来做你不愿做的事,这有多么危险? 浮游者挠其头. “我不知道。 我从来没有被问过。 长者灌顶. “每位牧师应准备回答这个问题。 如果做不到,他需要花一些时间祈祷和禁食,直到他能够做到为止。
舒适和自满是极其危险的。” 我受够了这些对话, 知道明智、健康的风险对教会的生活至关重要。 没有他们,教堂的奖杯。 它的存在原因导致了自我护理的崩溃,并在几年后变成了自我保护。 危险和坚硬的东西 让血流经身体 牧师,你负担不起海岸。
你买不起自动驾驶 你对耶稣和你的教会都有责任 在你的城市里充分利用机会, 这意味着除了传教、教义、祷告和发展领袖之外,你需要优先考虑为部委寻找新的途径。 做个福音企业家. 教会植树网早就认识到,创业能力对植树人至关重要。
但是,已经成立的教会——他们的牧师也需要创业吗? 福音企业家是什么? 牧师需要创业能力, 可能是因为我们想象有人不断发起他无法支撑的新事物,
如果这就是我们的意思,那么不,我们不希望我们的牧师成为企业家。 舒适和自满是极其危险的。 但福音企业家却不同 他不会堆积后脑勺的想法。 他保持清醒和清醒的头脑 关于上帝在社区中开启的机会。
他看到了新的发展过程的木框,并祈祷,一旦这些家庭搬进来,福音将如何到达他们手中。 他看着一些社区, 现有教堂无法深入所有人, 他为了把生长的教会植物移到一个更具战略意义的地点而拯救,施舍,牺牲.
他睁开眼睛,头脑锐利,手为上帝打开一扇门时刻做好准备. 圣经召唤 当这个话题出现时,人们通常会问,“你在哪里看到牧师在圣经中需要成为企业家?” 我的回答常常让人惊讶:耶稣以不诚实的经理为例。
在Luke 16:1–9中,一个富人发现他的房产经理在浪费他的财产,并告诉他结清账号——他即将被解雇。 经理意识到失去工作意味着挖掘或乞讨,所以他立即去工作切割交易,以获得其他富有雇主的青睐. 当他的雇主发现后,他赞扬经理的狡猾.
道德与否,这是一个天才的举动。 此时此刻,我们应该问,耶稣为什么讲这个故事? 也许他即将起诉经理这样的人。 但经理的不诚实与耶稣的观点无关. 曲折之处在于耶稣举起不诚实的经理作为他想要他的门徒们成为什么的例子.
“主人赞扬这位不诚实的经理的狡猾,”耶稣说。 " 因为这个世界的儿子在处理自己的一代时比光明的儿子们更精明"(公爵16:8). 譬喻如是叹. 世界的儿子们比我们更能抓住机会推进他们的王国, 含义是清醒的。
光之子们需要像关于暂时收益的世界一样 有意和机会性地谈论永恒 我们需要牧师,他们将祈祷 冒险,做艰难的事情, 感受紧迫感,抓住机会。 一个福音企业家保持清醒,清醒地思考上帝在社区中开启的机会. 这样想
Walmart和Target已经计划了 新的开发旁边的空地 数百万美元用于人口研究和营销运动, 你信不信由你, 可能有一个开发商 比你的教堂建筑 更有攻击性的想法。
我甚至听到一个故事, 说科罗拉多州的一座教堂正在死亡, 诸天子悉能扩张其国.
在跟随比喻的诗句中,耶稣将比喻与小事中的忠诚联系起来,很好地管理着大地资源,并记住我们为上帝服务,而不是我们的预算和资产. 作为牧师,我们的目标不是让我们的教友们快乐,靠捐赠维持生活,或维持机构最喜爱的捐赠者。
我们的工作是号召人们拾起十字架,跟随耶稣进入危险的机会,即使我们死了,人们也会看到耶稣. 不要规避风险 那个不诚实的经理知道 他没有时间反风险或自满 他不得不抓住一切机会拯救自己的皮肤. 牧师和教会也没有时间回避风险,
永无边劫. 牧师,做福音企业家。 当我们在最后一天站在我们的主面前时,也许世界的子孙对我们社会的影响比我们大。

articles.summary: Melissa and Courtney discuss how to cultivate discernment when seeking advice online and recognize the danger of letting AI or influencers replace wise counsel from the body of Christ.

articles.title_zh: 从互联网上获取建议的危险
articles.content: Melissa and Courtney discuss how to cultivate discernment when seeking advice. They talk about how sometimes we think we need information when what we really need is relationship. They discuss what kind of advice they like to get from the internet or ChatGPT, why they don’t recommend it for wisdom issues such as marriage and parenting, and why we shouldn’t let advice from AI or influencers replace wise counsel from the body of Christ. Resource Mentioned: Kitchen-Table Counseling Within Your Local Church Related Resources: Let’s Talk: Finding a Mentor and Being a Mentor Want to Grow in Wisdom? You Need Gospel Friends. Why AI Parenting Advice Falls Short Don’t Treat AI as Your Pastor Discussion Questions: 1. When you face a difficult decision or struggle, where do you typically turn for advice? 2. How do you discern whether online advice is helpful or unwise? 3. What makes advice offered within a personal relationship different from advice taken from an online blog or influencer or generated by AI? 4. How might repeated exposure to ideas about marriage, parenting, or relationships on social media influence our thinking without us being aware of it? 5. What do we lose when we turn to online sources for counsel instead of investing in relationships with people who know and love us? 6. Who in your life knows you well enough to speak honestly into your decisions and loves you enough to do so? How can you cultivate those kinds of relationships? 7. How would you like to grow in your ability to offer wise counsel to others?

articles.title: Beware Making Mental Illness an Identity
articles.summary: ‘All in Your Head’ is a concrete and compelling remapping of mental health culture with impressive explanatory power.
articles.summary_zh: 在他非自愿地被送入精神病院治疗两极分化后的几年里,弗雷德里克·德·博尔带着对挽救他生命的系统深表感谢和明显的沮丧,因为他的治愈经验变得如此罕见. 在你的脑海中:作为身份的疾病,作为时尚的创伤,以及希望陷入混乱,是互联网上最异形的思想家和作家之一的最新一面。 作为一位最以写作"聪明的邪教"而出名的"老派"马克思主义者,德博尔以自己的部落内部的文化漂移为目的,让那些最需要的人如此难以接受精神保健:"将精神疾病视为激动人心的冒险的倾向,在流行文化中无休止地浪漫化的放荡,是多年来我所照顾的诸多恶化之一"(8). 他的病情恶化的根源——将精神疾病和残疾视为一种值得庆贺的身份,而不是需要治疗的残疾——并不是他脑子里所有的东西。
articles.title_zh: 小心让精神疾病成为一种身份
articles.content: In the years since he was involuntarily committed to a mental health institution for bipolar disorder, Frederik deBoer has wrestled with both profound gratitude for a system that saved his life and also palpable frustration that his experience of healing has become so rare. All in Your Head: Illness as Identity, Trauma as Fashion, and the Desire to Be Disordered is the latest broadside from one of the internet’s most heterodox thinkers and writers. As an “old school” Marxist best known for writing The Cult of Smart , deBoer takes aim at how the cultural drift within his own tribe is responsible for making mental health care so elusive for those who need it most: “The tendency to treat mental illness as an exciting adventure, the endless romanticization of lunacy in popular culture, is one of many aggravations I have nursed for years” (8). The root of his aggravation—the treatment of mental illness and disability as an identity to be celebrated rather than a disability that needs treatment —isn’t all in his head. The use of talk therapy rose 47 percent between 2019 and 2024 . A 2025 LifeStance survey found around 29 percent of U.S. adults have self-diagnosed their mental health condition after consuming online content, rising to 50 percent among Gen Z (versus 9 percent of boomers). Of the people who self-diagnose symptoms, almost a quarter (24 percent) “rarely” or “never” feel the need to take the next step to discuss them with a qualified clinician. DeBoer argues that rather than reducing the stigma surrounding mental illness, the inordinate attention given to the mildly and dubiously afflicted is a dangerous distraction crowding out help for the severely ill. Accelerated by social media, this “gentrification of disability” has become a full-blown social contagion, compromising even the experts and institutions responsible for mental health care (153–54). DeBoer is largely right, and the cultural shift he identifies has real-world implications both inside and outside the church. But the same ideological priors that so sharpen deBoer’s critique also suffer from two significant blind spots that, were they addressed, would make All in Your Head the more courageous, more constructive, and, therefore, more widely read manifesto we need. General Bipartisan Ire If you picked up All in Your Head to understand how modern therapy culture spread like wildfire across social media over the last several years, it’s not immediately obvious why deBoer starts his argument with an in-depth analysis of the anti-psychiatry movement’s influence in late 20th century politics and academia. But, if you can forgive me the pun, there’s a method to his madness. After a blistering critique of “rightwing libertarian” policies that neglected mental illness, he cashes in on the subsequent trust he earns with left-leaning readers to launch a series of absolute haymakers toward “a species of thought that sometimes amounts to a kind of leftist pseudo-radicalism or a libertarian fantasy” (198) that drives the “destabilizing . . . move from mental illness as reality to mental illness as symbol” (8). American individualism and anti-institutional bias aren’t new, but the painstakingly specific way deBoer traces their spread through the culture surrounding mental health and therapy is refreshing and instructive. Our “apolitical romanticism of resistance to modern society” fuels two opposite errors: On the right, mental illness is sometimes seen as either imagined or a symptom of weak character. But on the left, the same romanticism often describes mental disability as more en abling than dis abling, as if neurodivergent minorities don’t need society’s help—society needs theirs. Gentrification of Disability DeBoer’s emphatic rejection of this predominantly progressive error— of “making a medical disorder an identity”—is the “overarching principle of [his] book” (165). This is never more clear in what he labels “the gentrification of disability,” where “diagnoses become fads” because the “intellectual and discursive space once dedicated to the interests of the most afflicted have become fixated instead on a class of patients whose disorders range from mild to dubious” (154). Said spaces and institutions have become so compromised due to “the diseased incentives of social media” and “liberal conventional wisdom that says it’s offensive to question any claim any individual makes about a disability.” Combined, “we’ve created ‘disorder communities’” not unlike fan clubs “rooting for a particular sports team” (154). The disproportionate attention given to those wealthy enough or high-functioning enough to perform their disability online is a dangerous distraction with real consequences: The more that influential elites use their status to “define the disorder in the public mind,” the more those who are impoverished or severely disabled go unseen and neglected. The disproportionate attention given to those wealthy enough or high-functioning enough to perform their disability online is a dangerous distraction with real consequences. Clear to anyone not living under a rock for the last decade is how familiar these patterns are. As I argued in The Reason for Church , counterfeit institutions (e.g., social media) have bypassed gatekeepers and hijacked the incentives of vital social and spiritual institutions undergirding American life. All in Your Head won’t add many new tools for recognizing these patterns. DeBoer’s contribution is in tracing them throughout an often convoluted bureaucratic ecosystem from the perspective of a “crabby old Marxist” frustrated by the privileged hypocrisy of pop-critical theory and progressive politics. However useful, the same ideological priors also handicap his analysis with two glaring omissions. Incomplete Diagnosis and Insufficient Prescription His most obvious omission is the rapid rise of gender dysphoria diagnoses and sex-reassignment surgery for minors. For more than a decade, gender-affirming physicians have been telling parents they must choose between having “a trans kid or a dead kid,” but, as Rebecca McLaughlin points out , the evidence says otherwise: “Puberty blockers can make the mental health of some young people worse, not better.” Considering deBoer’s impressive track record of taking unpopular, heterodox positions within his own tribe, his failure to address what is arguably the most volatile and life-altering consequence of toxic therapy culture is bewildering. DeBoer’s second omission is more understandable. While he concludes with well-reasoned (if regrettably materialist and socialist) policy prescriptions, he doesn’t offer any remedy for the broader therapeutic culture (i.e., the “ideological commitment to radical individual autonomy” [77]) that he spends most of the book arguing is the root of resistance to reform. That neglect robs his policy prescriptions of much persuasive power. Christians can affirm deBoer’s diagnosis of the problem of individual autonomy, but the church has the social and spiritual resources missing from all legislative and policy prescriptions. We know humans were never meant to construct our identities but to receive them in Christ and through belonging to our families, to our churches, and ultimately to God. Church has the social and spiritual resources missing from all legislative and policy prescriptions. Despite any omissions, All in Your Head is a clear-eyed and validating read, especially for those in (or disappointed by) mental health care. It would be a fine complement to Matthew Loftus’s Resisting Therapy Culture and describes many of the downstream problems Philip Rieff anticipated in The Triumph of the Therapeutic . All in Your Head is “not a memoir” (8) but a pragmatic antimemoir seething with a holy discontent that challenges both performative mental illness and the also voyeurism that incentivizes it. The result is a concrete and compelling remapping of mental health culture with impressive explanatory
articles.content_zh:
在他非自愿地被送入精神病院治疗两极分化后的几年里,弗雷德里克·德·博尔带着对挽救他生命的系统深表感谢和明显的沮丧,因为他的治愈经验变得如此罕见.
在你的脑海中:作为身份的疾病,作为时尚的创伤,以及希望陷入混乱,是互联网上最异形的思想家和作家之一的最新一面。
作为一位最以写作"聪明的邪教"而出名的"老派"马克思主义者,德博尔以自己的部落内部的文化漂移为目的,让那些最需要的人如此难以接受精神保健:"将精神疾病视为激动人心的冒险的倾向,在流行文化中无休止地浪漫化的放荡,是多年来我所照顾的诸多恶化之一"(8).
他的病情恶化的根源——将精神疾病和残疾视为一种值得庆贺的身份,而不是需要治疗的残疾——并不是他脑子里所有的东西。 2019年至2024年间,谈话疗法的使用率上升了47%. 2025年生活稳定调查发现美国约有29%的人口.
成人在消费在线内容后自行诊断其心理健康状况,在Gen Z中上升到了50%(相对于9%的繁荣者)。 在自我诊断的人群中,近四分之一(24%)的人“勉强”或“从未”感到有必要采取下一步措施,与合格的临床医生讨论这些症状。
DeBoer认为,对受轻度和可疑折磨的人的过度关注,与其减少精神疾病的污名化,不如说是一种危险的分心,挤出对重病患者的帮助。
社交媒体加速了这种 " 残疾意识化 " ,已成为一种全面的社会传染,甚至损害负责精神保健的专家和机构(153-54)。 DeBoer基本上是正确的,他所认定的文化转变在教堂内外都具有现实世界的影响.
但德布尔批评如此尖锐的意识形态前科也遭遇了两个重大盲点,如果这些盲点得到解决,将使你的头脑更加勇敢,更具建设性,因此,我们需要更广泛地阅读宣言。
一般两党爱尔兰人 如果你在脑海中看到现代治疗文化在过去几年里如何像野火一样在社交媒体上传播,那么DeBoer为什么以深入分析20世纪后期反精神病运动在政治和学术界的影响为出发点,这并不明显。
但是,如果你能原谅我的双关语,他疯狂是有办法的。
在对忽略了精神疾病的“右翼自由派”政策猛烈批评后,他依靠后来对左翼读者的信任,发动了一系列绝对的干草者,走向“有时相当于左翼伪激进主义或自由派幻想的思想”(198年),推动“稳定......”。
从精神疾病作为现实转变为精神疾病作为象征”(8)。 美国的个人主义和反机构偏见并非新事物, 但DeBoer通过精神卫生与治疗的文化,
我们“反对现代社会的政治浪漫主义”助长了两个相反的错误: 在右边,精神疾病有时被视为一种想象或一种弱性症状. 但是在左边,同样的浪漫主义常常将精神残疾描述为比分身更困难,仿佛神经分身的少数民族不需要社会的帮助——社会需要他们的帮助。
对DeBoer残疾人的强烈反对,即 " 使医疗障碍成为身份 " 这一主要进步的错误,是 " 书中的首要原则 " (165)。
在他所谓的“残疾的基因化”中,这一点再清楚不过了,因为“曾经专为受感染最深的人的利益服务的智慧和模糊空间已经固定在一类疾病从轻度到可疑的病人身上”(154个)。
因为“社会媒体的有病刺激”和“自由传统智慧, 综合起来, " 我们创建了`混乱社区 ' " ,与粉丝俱乐部 " 为某一特定体育队 " (154个)不同。
对足够富有或高运作能力的人的过度关注, 有影响力的上层人士越是利用其地位“界定公众心中的混乱”,穷人或严重残疾者就越是被忽视和忽视。
对那些足够富有或高功用、足以在线处理残疾的人的过度关注是一种危险的分心,会产生实际后果。 过去十年里没有生活在岩石下的人很清楚 这些模式是多么熟悉。
假冒机构(如社交媒体)绕过守门人, 并劫持了影响美国生活的重要社会及精神机构。 在你的脑海中,
DeBoer的贡献在于从一个被流行批评理论和进步政治的特有伪善所挫败的“疯狂的老马克思主义者”的视角来追踪整个经常被曲解的官僚生态系统。 不管多么有用,同样的意识形态前科也以两个明显的遗漏来阻碍他的分析。
未完全诊断和处方不足 他最明显的遗漏是性别障碍诊断和未成年人性转移手术的迅速上升.
十多年来,具有性别特征的医生一直告诉父母,他们必须在“一个跨性别的孩子或一个已经死亡的孩子”之间做出选择,但是,正如Rebecca McLaughlin所指出,证据却说道 : “ 纯洁的阻塞者可以使一些年轻人的精神健康恶化,而不是更好。 ” 考虑到德博尔在自己的部落中 占据不受欢迎的异教徒地位 令人印象深刻的记录
他未能解决毒药治疗文化 带来的最不稳定、最改变生命的后果, DeBoer的第二次遗漏更让人理解。
虽然他最后给出了合理(如果令人遗憾的是唯物主义和社会主义)政策处方,但他并没有为更广泛的治疗文化(即“激进个人自主的意识形态承诺”[77])提供任何补救,他花在书中的大部分争论是抵制改革的根源。 这种忽视剥夺了他的政策处方 很大的说服力。
基督徒可以肯定DeBoer对个人自治问题的诊断,但教会在所有立法和政策处方中都缺少社会和精神资源。 我们知道人类从来就不是要建立我们的身份,而是要在基督中,通过属于我们的家庭、我们的教会以及最终属于上帝来接受他们。
教会在所有立法和政策规定中都缺少社会和精神资源。 尽管有任何疏漏,但《你的头脑》是一个清晰而真实的读物,特别是对于接受(或因)精神保健的人来说。
并描述了Philip Rieff在《治疗的凯旋》中预料到的许多下游问题。 你脑子里全是“不是回忆录”(8),而是一种务实的预言,充满了圣洁的不满,既挑战了表现性精神疾病,也挑战了刺激这种疾病的巫术。
结果是以令人印象深刻的解释对心理健康文化进行了具体和令人信服的再规划。
articles.author: Brad Edwards

articles.title: How a Former Prisoner in Iran Wants You to Pray for Christians in Chains
articles.summary: Pray not only for what God might do for Christian prisoners in Iran but for what God might do through them, for his glory.
articles.summary_zh: 不久前,我和两名基督教青年在伊朗最困难的监狱之一服刑。 因为他们拒绝停止宣扬耶稣。 我问自己如何为他们祈祷, 他们说,“祈祷我们在这里的工作结束前不会被释放。 ”
articles.title_zh: 伊朗前囚犯如何希望你为被锁的基督徒祈祷
articles.content: Not long ago, I had a surreal phone call with two young Christian men serving prison sentences in one of Iran’s hardest prisons. They’re there because they refuse to stop preaching about Jesus. When I asked how I could pray for them, their answer wasn’t what you might expect. “Pray that we would not be released until our job here is finished,” they said. They had led numerous fellow prisoners to faith. Now, their chief concern was to remain inside long enough to disciple them. The call took me straight back to the five years I spent in prison for my faith. Now, these dear brothers (let’s call them Vahid and Reza) were behind bars, and I was outside. As we spoke, I pictured the wards and corridors, imagined the sounds and smells, and remembered how hard it was not to know how many years I would be there. But it was also an encouraging call. Vahid and Reza were in high spirits, talking about Bible passages that were sustaining them and how the Lord was at work. They didn’t see themselves in a miserable, dark place. They saw themselves in a different mission field. Their focus was the same as Paul’s in Colossians 4:3: “Pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to declare the mystery of Christ, on account of which I am in prison.” Paul’s request wasn’t for an open prison door but for an open door for the gospel. Pray for Gospel Fruit Vahid and Reza’s request resonated with me. I remember being unable to pray for my own release. I tried on a few occasions, but I couldn’t open my mouth to ask the Lord to release me. If I’m following Christ, I cannot choose the path. I cannot choose the location. I should follow him wherever he goes. And as I followed him to prison, he brought beautiful fruit. They didn’t see themselves in a miserable, dark place. They saw themselves in a different mission field. I think of one prisoner, a devout Muslim, who was wrongly accused of spying for Iran’s enemies. He was praying he would be released and was frustrated to get no answer. He approached me one day, saying, “Farshid, our God is dead. But I’ve heard yours is alive. Will you pray for me?” Fearing it might be a trap, I took him quietly aside and prayed briefly in the name of Jesus: “Lord, you know this man. Please hear his prayer.” The very next day, the man rushed over excitedly and gave me a huge hug. That morning, he had learned his name had been cleared. He was released two weeks later. Our God is indeed alive. The Lord was also at work softening my parents’ hearts toward Christ during those years. I always say that even if only for the salvation of my parents, my time in prison was worth it. So, when you pray for persecuted believers, pray not only for what God might do for them but—as Vahid and Reza requested—for what God might do through them, for his glory. Pray for gospel fruit. Pray for Comfort and Endurance I don’t want to make prison sound easier than it was. The suffering was real. So pray also for comfort and endurance. They beat me; they broke my toe. But the prolonged separation from my two children was the hardest burden to bear. The day I went to prison, my son was 2 years old and my daughter was 7. Missing their childhoods was an unspeakable loss. Yet I know others who have suffered much more than I did. I think of a brother currently in prison who has been tortured. I think of a sister who was sexually assaulted when she was arrested. Even the apostle Paul was at times “so utterly burdened beyond [his] strength that [he] despaired of life itself.” And his request to the church was simple: “You also must help us by prayer” (2 Cor. 1:8, 11). Brothers and sisters like these need us to pray for them with love. Whatever the situation, we can pray that God would grant the suffering believer comfort, peace, and endurance. The more specific the prayers, the better. While in prison, I received letters from people around the world who were praying for me. One wrote, “I am praying for your sleep. May the Lord give you peace to sleep well in prison.” I really loved it. And honestly, I did sleep well in prison; many inmates suffered from nightmares, but I cannot remember having a single one. I believe God answered that man’s prayers. Your Prayers Reach Through Prison Walls Prayer is especially needed when a prisoner is in solitary confinement. I spent 361 days in a solitary cell: For a year, I couldn’t see the sun in the sky. Yet prayers reached me through the prison walls. I remember one day I was in cell 73. I was sitting; I wasn’t praying. Suddenly, I was able to hear, let me say, a heavenly melody in my soul—not in my ears but in my soul. And I stood up. In that moment, I was overwhelmed by joy and peace. I started dancing. The cell was only two meters by two meters, but I danced before the Lord! The guard opened the door to see what I was doing. I turned to him with a wide smile and said, “Hey, sir, how are you today?” He looked at me with big eyes. “Wow, it seems you are better than me,” he said. And then he shut the door. For a year, I couldn’t see the sun in the sky. Yet prayers reached me through the prison walls. I believe someone, or maybe a group of people, was praying for me at that time. That’s why I had the experience of hearing that melody in my soul, and I was overwhelmed by joy, even though I was in solitary confinement. Many brothers and sisters around the world prayed for me during my imprisonment. Perhaps you were one of them. I cannot find the words to say thank you. Now, I want to ask, Will you pray for those in prison right now for their faith? Scripture tells us to “remember those who are in prison, as though in prison with them” (Heb. 13:3). I believe your prayer goes through the prison walls. It can touch the prisoners, encourage them, and give them joy while they’re suffering, because it’s possible to have joy and suffering at the same time. Vahid and Reza are just two of the Christians in Iran’s prisons today. There are so many. Maybe you’re asking, Where do I start? Elam’s free Bound Together resources can help your church or small group pray on the International Day of Prayer for the Persecuted Church on November 1. We pray because our God is faithful to his children. He is faithful right now to Vahid and Reza and to all our brothers and sisters in prison. And he was faithful to me. When I came out of prison, people would say to me, “Praise God, Farshid, you were faithful to the Lord. You stood for the Lord.” I always try to correct them. That’s not true. He was faithful to me. He stood for me.

不久前,我和两名基督教青年在伊朗最困难的监狱之一服刑。 因为他们拒绝停止宣扬耶稣。 我问自己如何为他们祈祷, 他们说,“祈祷我们在这里的工作结束前不会被释放。”
他们带领许多同狱囚犯信仰。 现在,他们最关心的是 留在里面的时间足够长 让他们入门。 那通电话把我带回我为信仰在监狱里度过的五年。 现在,这些亲爱的兄弟(让我们叫他们Vahid和Reza)在监狱里,我在外面。
就在我们发言的时候,我想象了病房和走廊,想象了声音和气味,并想起了不知道我会在那里呆了多少年是多么困难。 但这也是一个令人鼓舞的呼吁。 瓦希德和礼萨精神高尚,谈论着支撑着他们的圣经段落,以及上帝是如何工作的. 他们并没有看到自己在一个悲惨而黑暗的地方。
他们看到自己在另一个任务领域。 他们的重心与保罗在Colosisans 4:3中的重心相同 : “ 也为我们祈祷,以便上帝为我们打开一个话语之门,宣告基督之谜,我为此而入狱。 ” 保罗的要求并不是打开监狱的门, 祈求福音果实Vahid,
我还记得我无法为自己的自由祈祷 我尝试过几次, 我无法选择道路。 我无法选择位置 我该跟着他 不管他去哪 当我跟着他进监狱时 他带来了美丽的水果 他们并没有看到自己在一个悲惨而黑暗的地方。
他们看到自己在另一个任务领域。 我想到一个囚犯, 一个虔诚的穆斯林, 他祈祷自己会被释放,并因得不到答复而感到沮丧。 有一天,他靠近我说,“法尔希德,我们的神死了。 但我听说你还活着。
你会为我祈祷吗?” 我担心那可能是一个陷阱,悄悄地把他放在一旁,以耶稣的名义简短地祈祷道:"主啊,你认识这个人。 请听他的祈祷。” 第二天,那个男人激动地冲过来,给了我一个巨大的拥抱。 那天早晨,他得知自己的名字已被清除。 他两周后被释放。 我们的神确实还活着。
在那些年中,上帝也在努力使我父母对基督的心软化。 我总是说,即使只是为了拯救我的父母, 我在监狱的时间是值得的。 当你们祈祷受迫害的信士们的时候,你们应当祈祷真主所意欲者,犹如瓦希德和里萨所意欲者那样,祈祷真主所意欲者。 祈取福音果实.
祈祷舒适与耐力, 苦难是真实的。 因此也祈求安慰和耐力. 他们打我,把我的脚趾弄断了 但是,与我的两个孩子长期分离是最难承受的负担。 我入狱那天,我的儿子2岁,女儿7岁。 失去童年是一个难以形容的损失。
然而,我认识其他人,他们遭受的痛苦比我多得多。 我想到目前在监狱里的一个兄弟 曾遭受酷刑 我想到一个妹妹在被捕时曾被性侵犯. 甚至使徒保罗,有时也“承受了超过他力量的沉重负担,以致于他对生命本身绝望”。 他向教堂提出的要求很简单:“你还必须通过祈祷帮助我们”(第1:8、11节)。
这样的兄弟姐妹需要我们用爱为他们祈祷. 无论情况如何,我们可以祈祷上帝会给予受苦受难的信徒以安慰、和平和耐力。 祈祷越具体越好 在狱中,我收到了世界各地为我祈祷的人的来信。 有人写道:“我在为你的睡眠祈祷。
愿主赐予你和平,让你在狱中安眠。” 我真的很喜欢 老实说,我在狱中睡得还不错,许多囚犯都遭受了噩梦,但我不记得有过一次噩梦。 我相信上帝回答了他的祈祷。 当囚犯被单独监禁时,特别需要你的祈祷书。
我在一个单独牢房里度过了361天:一年来, 然而祈祷通过监狱的墙壁来到了我。 我记得有天我在73号牢房里 我坐在一旁, 突然间,我得以听到,让我说,我的灵魂中充满了天堂的旋律——不是在我耳朵中,而是在我的灵魂中。 我站起来。 在那一刻,我被欢乐与和平所淹没。 我开始跳舞。
牢房只有两米一两米 但我在主面前跳舞! 卫所开出门来见我所为. 我大笑地对他说,“先生,你今天好吗?” 他用大眼睛看着我 “哇,看来你比我好,”他说。 然后他关了门。 一年来,

我找不到话要说谢谢。 现在,我想问,你会祈祷 那些在监狱里的人现在的信仰? 圣经告诉我们,“记住那些在狱中的人,好像在狱中一样”(Heb. 13:3)。 我相信你的祈祷会穿过监狱的墙壁

articles.title: CNN says a ‘tsunami’ of church closings is coming. The data says otherwise
articles.summary: A recent CNN article warned that a “tsunami” of church closings is poised to remake America. But the numbers tell a quieter story. Closures barely outpace openings, and the most alarming figure counts sold buildings, not dying congregations.
articles.summary_zh: 美国有线电视新闻网（ CNN ）最近的一篇文章警告说，教堂关闭的“海啸”将重塑美国。但这些数字讲述了一个更安静的故事。关闭的速度几乎超过了开口，最令人担忧的数字是出售的建筑物，而不是垂死的会众。
articles.title_zh: 美国有线电视新闻网（ CNN ）表示，教堂关闭的“海啸”即将来临。数据显示并非如此

articles.title: Christians with PTSD: Why fear doesn’t mean weak faith
articles.summary: For six years, a deacon took back roads to avoid the interstate where a truck hit him. He believed his fear meant he didn’t trust God enough. Clinical psychologist David Zuccolotto explains why that belief is wrong and what finally helped him drive again.
articles.summary_zh: 六年来，一名执事为了避开一辆卡车撞到他的州际公路，抢回了公路。他认为他的恐惧意味着他不够信任上帝。临床心理学家David Zuccolotto解释了为什么这种信念是错误的，以及最终帮助他再次开车的原因。
articles.title_zh: 患有创伤后应激障碍的基督徒：为什么恐惧并不意味着信仰软弱
articles.author: David Zuccolotto

articles.title: Art Programs in Lebanon Bring Beauty to Midst of Crisis
articles.summary: With Lebanon currently being impacted by war, a refugee crisis, and more, stories of beauty can be hard to come across. For ministries active in Lebanon, meeting the spiritual, physical...
articles.summary_zh: 黎巴嫩目前受到战争、难民危机以及更多难民的影响, 对活跃在黎巴嫩的各部来说,满足一个国家的精神、身体和情感需要,只是为了生存而努力,是会付出代价的。 Horizons International的Pierre Houssney说,尽管由于人类在罪恶世界中的堕落,国家仍然面临创伤,但上帝仍然创造了一个充满美丽的世界。 “我认为,美丽对人们的心来说是关于上帝的,特别是当它不仅仅是为了美丽,而是以基督的名义的美丽时。 ”
articles.title_zh: 黎巴嫩的艺术项目将美丽带入危机
articles.content: With Lebanon currently being impacted by war, a refugee crisis, and more, stories of beauty can be hard to come across. For ministries active in Lebanon, meeting the spiritual, physical and emotional needs of a country just trying to survive can take its toll. Horizons International’s Pierre Houssney said that despite the trauma the country faces due to the fallenness of man in a sinful world, God has still created a world that contains beauty. “And I think that beauty speaks to people’s hearts about God, especially when it’s not just beauty, you know, for beauty’s sake, but when it’s beauty in the name of Christ,” Houssney said. “In the midst of the trauma, in the midst of the poverty, we’re trying to give opportunities for believers, who have artistic gifts, to have a prophetic voice through their art to the society, so that we can be calling out for Christ in the midst of the crisis.” Some of these opportunities for creating beauty are fine art classes offered by Horizons International. Horizons International has had up to 35 students at one time participating in these classes revolving around painting or drawing. Students in visual arts classes had the opportunity to participate in an exhibition in Beirut called “His Touch.” People from the community were invited to see the work of beginner students as well as 10 different Christian artists. Graphic design classes offer a more practical element, allowing students to learn a skill they could use in their everyday lives. On the worship side of things, music theory and classes in instruments are helping raise up worship leaders for local churches. One unit teaching guitar, piano, and drums to beginners looking to lead worship at their church had 70 people participate. “And so this new generation needs training, and they need, you know, they need mentoring, and they need to have those skills so that they can, they can lead their congregations in worship,” Houssney said. Though some may have more trouble connecting visual arts directly with ministry, Houssney says social media helps make that connection more clear. Beautiful videos that contain scripture messages alongside visual art tend to get a higher viewership. When posts like that get more views, they can potentially bring more people to Christ. “And so it needs to be beautiful. It needs to be excellent, it needs to be well done. And that’s what our Lord deserves,” Houssney said. “That’s not just what social media deserves.” Currently, Horizons International has to spread resources between humanitarian aid like food and medicine and projects that glorify God through the arts. In the midst of the crisis in Lebanon, pray for God to provide the resources for canvases, studio spaces, art instructors and more. Houssney also says what an organization like Horizons International is here for is to see God open more and more hearts to the Gospel. “So I’m not praying that the church would have less hardship. I’m not praying for you know, for less, you know, political chaos. What I’m praying for is that, through it all, people would continue to open their hearts, and that God will be glorified.” Learn more about the work of Horizons International in Lebanon by visiting https://www.horizonsinternational.org/lebanon-crisis .
articles.content_zh:
黎巴嫩目前受到战争、难民危机以及更多难民的影响, 对活跃在黎巴嫩的各部来说,满足一个国家的精神、身体和情感需要,只是为了生存而努力,是会付出代价的。
Horizons International的Pierre Houssney说,尽管由于人类在罪恶世界中的堕落,国家仍然面临创伤,但上帝仍然创造了一个充满美丽的世界。 “我认为,美丽对人们的心来说是关于上帝的,特别是当它不仅仅是为了美丽,而是以基督的名义的美丽时。”
“在创伤中,在贫困中,我们正试图给有艺术天赋的信徒机会,通过他们的艺术向社会发出预言的声音,以便在危机中呼唤基督。” 其中一些创造美貌的机会是地平线国际提供的精美艺术课.
Horizons International曾经有多达35名学生参加这些围绕绘画或绘画的课. 在贝鲁特举办的名为“他的触摸”的展览。 社区人士应邀观看初学者以及10位不同的基督教艺术家的作品.
图形设计课提供了一个更实用的元素,让学生学习他们日常生活中可以使用的技能. 在事物的崇拜方面,乐器中的音乐理论和课程帮助培养地方教会的崇拜领袖. 一个教吉他,钢琴,和鼓的单位,在他们的教堂里寻找引领崇拜的初学者,有70人参加.
“因此,这新一代需要培训,他们需要,你知道,他们需要指导,他们需要这些技能,以便他们能够领导他们的教会进行礼拜。” 虽然有些人可能更难直接将视觉艺术与部委联系起来,
包含经文信息与视觉艺术的美丽视频往往获得更高的收视率. 当这样的帖子获得更多的观点时,它们有可能将更多的人带到基督身边. “因此,它必须是美丽的。 它需要出色,需要做得好。 这才是我们的主应得的。
“这不仅仅是社交媒体应得的。 目前,地平线国际必须在食品和药品等人道主义援助和通过艺术赞美上帝的项目之间分配资源。 在黎巴嫩危机中,祈求上帝为画布、工作室空间、艺术指导员等提供资源。
霍斯尼还说,象地平线国际这样的组织在这里是为了看到上帝对福音书的开放越来越多. 「所以我不祈祷教会会减少困难。 我不是在为你们祈祷,
我祈祷的是,通过这一切,人们将继续敞开心扉,上帝将受到赞美。” 透过访问https://www.horizonsinternational.org/lebanon-crisis,

articles.title_zh: v.容忍
articles.content: This incident took place over 15 years ago, and yet, I remember it clearly.  In the buzz of daily life, it is easy to get caught up in the carelessness of the checklists, and forget the intentionality of abiding in Him. I remember how frantic I was once at or late deadline and how frustrated I was at all the problems we were having in getting the program together.  We’d all kinds of equipment failure throughout the day and I was going to have to drive the program across town to get it uploaded to the satellite.  It was already 7 pm and the babysitter was calling me every 10 minutes. Then, I got a call from a lady with a gentle Creole accent. She told me, “I felt led to call you and pray with you.”  I SO didn’t want to talk to this lady, wasn’t interested in being prayed over, and really just wanted to leave to get this program fed and pick my 2-year old up.  I was impatient when I responded to her.  Rather than take insult from what was probably a curt rebuff,  she just said , “Wow. You REALLY need the peace of our heavenly Father on your heart right now.” And…she burst out in song.   Now I’m wondering why I’m on the phone with this crazy lady, and then she prayed through the worship song and then rolled right into praying for me, for my distress, for the things I thought I needed to do…and prayed that I would be still and listen, that my heart would be quiet long enough to remember the awe of God, and that the joy would come back to my heart as we produced MNN… The more she prayed, the more convicted I grew and I realized I was caught up in the ‘do’ and not the ‘be’…and THEN she pulled out the big guns: the story of Mary and Martha. Luke 10:38-42 New International Version (NIV) At the Home of Martha and Mary 38 As Jesus and his disciples were on their way, he came to a village where a woman named Martha opened her home to him. 39 She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to what he said. 40 But Martha was distracted by all the preparations that had to be made. She came to him and asked, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister has left me to do the work by myself? Tell her to help me!” 41 “Martha, Martha,” the Lord answered, “you are worried and upset about many things, 42 but few things are needed—or indeed only one. [ a ] Mary has chosen what is better, and it will not be taken away from her.” She ended our conversation with, “Sometimes, it’s ok to be Mary and sit at the feet of Jesus.  Stuff will still be there to do. It will eventually get done.  But the lasting investment is remembering to sit and BE at the feet of Jesus.” It was a much needed gentle rebuke along with a little encouragement from an unknown sister in Christ that I still remember to this day…thousands of productions later.   What we do is important…but not at the risk of forgetting to abide in Christ.

articles.title_zh: Koinonia
articles.content: Koinonia (Koy-no-nee’-ah) is a Greek word, occurring 20 times in the Bible, which means “fellowship” or “brotherly love.” It carries with it the meaning of a committed, trustworthy, and dependable relationship. Such a relationship can be experienced through participation, sharing, giving, and contributing. The first occurrence of koinonia is Acts 2:42 “They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.” But the rest of the passage reads:  “ 43 Everyone was filled with awe at the many wonders and signs performed by the apostles. 44 All the believers were together and had everything in common. 45 They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. 46 Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, 47 praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.” Christian fellowship is a key aspect of the Christian life. Believers in Christ are to come together in love, faith, and encouragement. The essence of koinonia: “one another”. Scripture commands us to be devoted to one another (Romans 12:10), honor one another (Romans 12:10), live in harmony with one another (Romans 12:16; 1 Peter 3:8), accept one another (Romans 15:7), serve one another in love (Galatians 5:13), be kind and compassionate to one another (Ephesians 4:32), admonish one another (Colossians 3:16), encourage one another (1 Thessalonians 5:11; Hebrews 3:13), spur one another on toward love and good deeds (Hebrews 10:24), offer hospitality (1 Peter 4:9), and love one another (1 Peter 1:22; 1 John 3:11; 3:23; 4:7; 4:11-12). Koinonia is translated many different ways in English Bibles: -fellowship (koinonia), to the breaking of bread and the prayers.” -contribution (koinonia) for them and for all others.” Paul writes to the believers in Philippi: “That I may know him and the power of his resurrection, and may share (koinonia) his sufferings, becoming like him in his death” (Phil 3:10). – Christian living– the dynamic whole of it. It describes an interactive relationship between God and believers who are sharing new life through Christ.  It captures the entirety of this relationship. It involves active participation in Christian community: sharing in spiritual blessings and giving material blessings. How does this idea fit into the theology of ‘And’? Acts 1:8—it empowers us with the chisomo—the grace to DO—the all-inclusive– “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.” And they will know you by your love.  (John 13:35)   “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”
articles.content_zh:
Koinonia(Koy-no-nee-ah)是一个希腊语词汇,在圣经中出现20次,意思是"fellowship"或"兄弟之爱". 它带有坚定、可信和可靠的关系的意义。 这种关系可以通过参与、分享、给予和贡献来经历。
韩国最早发生的是2:42法案 " 他们致力于使徒的教诲和奖学金、断面包和祈祷。 " 但该段落的其余部分写道:“43个人对使徒们所完成的许多奇迹和标志充满了敬畏。 44,所有信徒都在一起,拥有一切共同之处.
45 他们出售财产和财产,给任何有需要的人。 46 他们每天继续在寺庙法庭开会。 他们在家中砸碎面包,与欢乐和真诚的心一起吃,47人赞美上帝,享受全体人民的恩惠.
真主天天增加他们中被拯救者的人数。 基督教研究金是基督教生活的一个关键方面。 信仰基督的信徒们将聚在爱、信仰和鼓励中。 koinonia的本质是:“一个”。 圣经命令我们互相奉献(罗姆人12:10),互相尊崇(罗姆人12:10),彼此和睦相处(罗姆人12:16);
1 Peter 3 : 8) 相互接受(罗马人15:7) 互相爱慕(加拉提人5:13) 彼此友善和慈悲(伊菲斯人4:32) 相互劝告(科洛斯人3:16) 相互鼓励(1 Thessalonians 5:11;希伯来人3:13) 相互激励爱与善行(希伯来人10:24) 给予款待(1:彼得4:9) 相互爱护(1:彼得1:22;1:约翰3:11);
3:23;4:7;4:11-12). 科伊诺尼亚在英语圣经中翻译了许多不同的方式:-fellowship(koinonia),用于断面包和祈祷。” 保罗对菲利皮的信徒写道:“以便我了解他及其复活的力量,并分享他的痛苦,使他在死亡中变得像他一样”(Phil 3:10)。
- 基督教生活 - 充满活力的全部。 它描述了上帝和通过基督分享新生活的信徒之间的互动关系. 它捕捉了这种关系的全部内容. 它涉及积极参与基督教社区:分享精神祝福和物质祝福。 这个想法如何融入“和”的神学?
行动1:8——它能使我们获得至仁主的恩惠——“当圣灵降临你的时候,你将获得权力;你将成为我在耶路撒冷、整个犹太教和撒马利亚的见证,以及大地的尽头。” 他们会知道你的爱。 (John 13:35)说:不然,人人都知道你们是我的门徒,如果你们相爱。

There is something of music in the very sound of these words. The thought that lies below them, sweeping as it does through the whole creation, and parting all things into the transient and eternal, the mortal and immortal, is still greater than the music of the words. ‘These’ are removed; ‘this’ abides.

articles.title_zh: 契  约
articles.content: Isaiah 54:10  Though the mountains be shaken and the hills be removed, yet my unfailing love for you will not be shaken nor my covenant of peace be removed,” says the LORD, who has compassion on you. There is something of music in the very sound of these words. The thought that lies below them, sweeping as it does through the whole creation, and parting all things into the transient and eternal, the mortal and immortal, is still greater than the music of the words. ‘These’ are removed; ‘this’ abides. The thing in God which abides is all-gentle tenderness, that strange love mightier than all the powers of Deity beside, permanent with the permanence of His changeless heart. ‘My loving kindness and the covenant of My peace,’ outlast everything else. The antithesis of what passes and what abides is mind-boggling. ‘all things are in a state of flux’—it’s a basic tenant of physical science…and yet it seems as unchanging as anything we know…it’s the shape of the box…and yet,  if we had nothing abiding beyond this universe, what would be the point? There’s an unspoken  ‘But’  here–  in that vacuum, the Great Spirit moves all the material universe, Himself unmoved, undiminished by creation, or by said vacuum.  The Unknowable whose name means ‘breath’ is YHWH—who comes to us in man-form to help the created move toward and abide in this presence. I’m sort of blown away by how big this passage paints God…and blown away that we are His children…and that we able to abide because of Christ…that our part in glorifying Him and enjoying Him forever comes in walking alongside a global family and telling their stories.  Insignificant, by itself, but being used as a tool to help others abide and recognize the mercy and grace of this big Abba. We can touch the face of God…because He calls us to Himself.
articles.content_zh:
以赛亚54:10 虽然山岳被震动,山丘被移走,但我对你们的爱是不会动摇的,我的和约是不会解除的,"对你们有慈悲的耶和华说: 这些话的音响中有些音乐
在他们下面的思绪,如它横扫着整个创造,把一切分化为短暂和永恒的,凡人和不朽的,仍然比文字的音乐更伟大. `这些'将被删除;`这'将永存。
神所坚持的,是万能的温柔, 奇怪的爱比神的一切力量更强大, 与神的永恒的 不变的心。 我的慈爱和平安的盟约,超过万物。 所经过的和所坚持的反面是思维混乱。
”所有的事情都处于通量的状态, 这是物理科学的基本租借者. 这里有一个未言而喻的“但是 ” — — 在这个真空中,伟大精神移动了所有的物质宇宙,它自己没有移动,不受创造或上述真空的伤害。
名叫`呼吸 ' 的不知名者是YHWH,他以人形来到我们身边,帮助创造出来的人类走向,并在此存在中坚持下去。
也因为基督而得以遵守。 我们赞美他, 享受他, 本身并不重要,但被用作帮助他人遵守和承认这个大阿巴的慈悲和恩惠的工具.
我们可以触摸上帝的面孔... 因为他叫我们自己。

articles.title_zh: Innocent As Doves
articles.content: The Scriptures Ephesians 6:10-18 (NIV) 10 Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. 11 Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes. 12 For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. 13 Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand. 14 Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place, 15 and with your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace. 16 In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one. 17 Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit,which is the word of God. 18 And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people. Matthew 10:16-20 16 “I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves. 17 Be on your guard; you will be handed over to the local councils and be flogged in the synagogues. 18 On my account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.19 But when they arrest you, do not worry about what to say or how to say it. At that time you will be given what to say, 20 for it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.” Today, it’s just been on my mind to bring our attention back to the armor of God and the fact we need to be wise like serpents, innocent as doves. I want to speak to the first part, being wise like serpents. Going to Malta helped bring to my attention how much I don’t know about my own country’s politics, the refugee crisis, trusting God, and even God’s word. I feel like I’m doing “better than the average U.S. citizen.” But, in reality, I don’t know very much. And I’ve realized when it comes to engaging in conversation with others, it’s important to have a handle on topics like these. I.e., talking with my dad about refugees. Having facts and knowing the what the constitution says helps me to better articulate and defend my stance culturally and based by our country’s laws. Knowing about the situation with refugees abroad also helps and is a tool in dispelling the fear which the current administration seems to use to get support to make the calls it’s trying to make both about refugees and immigrants in general. The second part, being innocent like doves…that’s a hard one for me because I’ve thought in the past it means to be naive. I don’t want to be naïve. But being innocent doesn’t mean you’re naïve. I think it means we guard our hearts and take our thoughts captive. What we put into our minds affects the lens through which we see the world and view the Bible—and it has the power to jade us. I.e., rape. I know rape is in the world. I know it is destructive. I’ve seen it damage lives. And I’ve seen God redeem. But, what I don’t need to do is read the part of a book or watch a TV series which details a situation of rape. I don’t need to invite that in my mind to “know” about rape. I’m thinking of a book one of my youth group girls was reading. I haven’t read it, but I see how she struggles with her sexuality, her relationship with God, and for a period even suicide. I also see how her parents are okay with exposing her to things that are a bit mature for her age. Compared to another one of our girls who is aware of what happens in the world, but her parents are careful to protect her from exposure to things which are dark, damaging, fracture her relationship with God. She’s being taught to be innocent, not naïve (or judgmental), and to take her thoughts captive. Both of these girls come from solid Christian homes. I can’t say for sure that what each of these girls has or hasn’t been exposed to has been the big factor in who they are today, but I think it’s clear it has played a role. No barely 12-year-old girl should be reading intimate details about sex or rape. And while I may think not allowing your 12-year-old to watch Harry Potter could be a little excessive, I see how this other young girl is being shaped to cast her thoughts on what is good and to pursue God in all things. Which leads me to the Armor of God. If we are sheep among wolves, if we are God’s people aware of the spiritual battle around us, we need the armor of God. We need our faith, especially when we don’t have answers to why God is still good in hard situations, but know that he is. We need the encouragement of salvation when doubt comes into our minds if we are truly loved by God. We need to know the scriptures, not just where to find them in the Bible, but to really be so in-tuned we can recite them when necessary. We need the breastplate of righteousness because frankly, the world is watching. And with the armor of God and I think it’s important to ask, do we believe in spiritual warfare? Do we believe the world we live in isn’t just made up of cold, hard facts or only what we can see? When I was talking about spiritual warfare with my friend who’s in Ecuador, she mentioned how we leave ourselves open to it. Every morning we can either be aware that it’s there and pray, or we can disregard it and leave ourselves open. Praying against spiritual warfare isn’t just for the days when we can sense it, but even when we don’t suspect it. With all of this said, I want to encourage each of us to really grab hold of the scriptures, of God, and for what it means to put on God’s armor as well as to be wise like serpents, but innocent as doves.
articles.content_zh:
圣经以弗所书6:10-18(NIV)10 最后,在主和他的强大力量中要坚强. 11,穿上上帝的全盔甲,以便你能够站出来反抗魔鬼的阴谋. 12,因为我们的斗争不是反对血肉,而是反对统治者,反对当局,反对这个黑暗世界的力量,反对天界邪恶的精神力量.
13,因此穿上神的全甲,以便当邪恶之日来临时,你能够站稳脚跟,在做了一切之后,站稳脚跟. 14 站稳脚跟,把真理带系在腰上,把正义的胸罩摆好,15 和你的脚固定在和平的福音中。
16,除此之外,还要拿起信仰的盾牌,用这个盾牌可以扑灭邪恶者的所有火箭. 17,拿救世之盔,取灵剑,即神话. 18,并在各种场合以各种祈祷和请求在精神中祈祷. 记住这一点,保持警惕,永远为主的所有人民祈祷。
马修 10: 16-20 16 “我派遣你们同狼群中的羊一样。 因此,要像蛇一样精明,像鸽子一样无辜. 17 个 人 守 着 、 交给 地方 议会 、 在 犹太会堂 被 鞭打
18,就我而言,你们将被带见总督和国王,作为他们和外邦人的见证。 19,但当他们逮捕你时,不要担心该说什么或者怎么说.
在那日,你们得享受你们所应当享受的恩惠,20个不是你们所应当享受的,而是你们父亲的精神。 今天,我正想着让我们重新关注神的盔甲, 以及我们需要像蛇一样的聪明, 我想说第一部分, 像蛇一样聪明。
我对本国政治、难民危机、信任上帝、甚至上帝之言一无所知。 我觉得自己比普通美国公民做得更好。 但事实上, 我意识到,在与其他人对话时,必须处理这类议题。
和我爸谈难民的事 了解事实,了解宪法的内容,有助于我更好地阐明和捍卫我的立场。
了解国外难民情况也有助于消除现政府似乎用来获得支持的恐惧, 第二部分是像鸽子一样无辜, 我不想天真。
但无辜并不意味着你天真。 我认为这意味着我们保护我们的心 并抓住我们的思想。 我们脑海中的东西 影响着我们看到世界和看《圣经》的镜头 并且它有制玉的力量 强奸 我知道强奸在世界上。 我知道这是破坏性的。 我亲眼看到它会伤害生命。 我见过上帝赎罪。
我并不需要读书或看电视连续剧, 我并不需要邀请她去“了解”强奸。 我想到一本我的青年团体女孩读的书。 她的性爱、与上帝的关系, 甚至自杀,
我也明白她的父母 把她暴露在 对她这个年龄来说有点成熟的东西上有什么用 和另外一位我们的女孩相比,她知道世界上发生的事情,但她的父母很小心地保护她免受那些黑暗,有害,断裂她与上帝关系的事情的影响.
她被教导自己是无辜的,而不是天真的(或判断性的),并俘虏她的思想。 这两个女孩都来自坚固的基督教家庭. 我无法肯定每个女孩是否曾接触过她们,
任何12岁的女孩都不应该读到关于性或强奸的亲密细节。 虽然我可能认为不允许你12岁的孩子看《哈利波特》可能有点过分, 但我知道这个年轻女孩是如何被塑造的, 将她的想法投射到什么是好的, 并在万物中追求上帝。 这让我找到神的盔甲
如果我们是狼群中的羊,如果我们是上帝的人民,知道我们周围的精神斗争,我们需要上帝的盔甲。 我们需要我们的信仰, 尤其是当我们没有答案, 如果我们真的受到上帝的爱,我们需要在出现疑问时得到拯救的鼓励。
我们需要知道这些经文, 不仅仅是在圣经中找到它们的地方, 而且为了真正地调和,我们在必要时可以朗诵它们。 我们需要正义的胸罩 因为坦率地说,世界在看着。 我们相信精神战争吗?
我们是否相信我们所生活的世界, 我和在厄瓜多尔的朋友谈论精神战争时, 每天早上,我们要么意识到它的存在,要么祈祷,要么我们无视它,敞开心扉。
祈祷反抗精神战不仅仅是我们感应到的年代, 我想鼓励我们每个人 真正抓住经文,上帝, 以及赋予上帝盔甲的意义,

articles.title_zh: 亚伯拉罕和洛特
articles.content: Genesis 13 So Abram left Egypt and traveled north into the Negev, along with his wife and Lot and all that they owned. 2 (Abram was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold.) 3 From the Negev, they continued traveling by stages toward Bethel, and they pitched their tents between Bethel and Ai, where they had camped before. 4 This was the same place where Abram had built the altar, and there he worshiped the Lord again. 5 Lot, who was traveling with Abram, had also become very wealthy with flocks of sheep and goats, herds of cattle, and many tents. 6 But the land could not support both Abram and Lot with all their flocks and herds living so close together. 7 So disputes broke out between the herdsmen of Abram and Lot. (At that time Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land.) 8 Finally Abram said to Lot, “Let’s not allow this conflict to come between us or our herdsmen. After all, we are close relatives! 9 The whole countryside is open to you. Take your choice of any section of the land you want, and we will separate. If you want the land to the left, then I’ll take the land on the right. If you prefer the land on the right, then I’ll go to the left.” 10 Lot took a long look at the fertile plains of the Jordan Valley in the direction of Zoar. The whole area was well watered everywhere, like the garden of the Lord or the beautiful land of Egypt. (This was before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.) 11 Lot chose for himself the whole Jordan Valley to the east of them. He went there with his flocks and servants and parted company with his uncle Abram. 12 So Abram settled in the land of Canaan, and Lot moved his tents to a place near Sodom and settled among the cities of the plain. 13 But the people of this area were extremely wicked and constantly sinned against the Lord. 14 After Lot had gone, the Lord said to Abram, “Look as far as you can see in every direction—north and south, east and west. 15 I am giving all this land, as far as you can see, to you and your descendants[a] as a permanent possession. 16 And I will give you so many descendants that, like the dust of the earth, they cannot be counted! 17 Go and walk through the land in every direction, for I am giving it to you.” 18 So Abram moved his camp to Hebron and settled near the oak grove belonging to Mamre. There he built another altar to the Lord. At this point in the story, God’s promise to Abraham of the promised land hasn’t come true yet, but good land is part of the promise We’ve seen Abraham have faithful triumphs and failures, but this is a time when Abraham showed great faith once again because there are SEVERAL reasons why Abraham could have taken the better land 1. movement towards God’s promise of good land anyway 2. and this is probably a more striking one to me, but culturally speaking, the older would NEVER defer to the younger. Lot, as the younger, should have deferred to Abraham the older – both in going to him to resolve the disagreement between their herdsmen and in giving him the better pick of land But Abraham wasn’t fixated on culture and on manipulating God’s promises Abraham’s dealings are not in seniority, but in brotherly love and that’s what faith does. Faith resolves tension with generous self-sacrifice Christians often say in tense situations, “Well, I’m not a doormat! I deserve not to be walked all over!” But my pastor said something very striking to me. “Aren’t we glad Christ never said that?” A faithful and generous person doesn’t need to manipulate or control the situation because they are resting in the promises and sovereignty of God Faith leads to trust leads to generosity and self-sacrifice with others.

articles.title: Best Practices from Evangelistically Effective Churches
articles.summary: While thousands of Americans are dechurching, some churches are baptizing many new members. Here’s how the country’s most evangelistically effective churches are sharing the gospel.
articles.summary_zh: https://media. thegospelcoalition. org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2310213/ 有效-福音主义. mp3 2021年夏天,牧师卢克·彼得森搬到俄亥俄州哥伦布寻找失落的人.
articles.title_zh: 传福音有效教会的最佳实践
articles.content: https://media.thegospelcoalition.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/23102213/effective-evangelism.mp3 In the summer of 2021, pastor Luke Peterson moved to Columbus, Ohio, to look for lost people. To find them, he joined a gym. He started building friendships. And then he began asking those friends if they wanted to come over. “Word started getting around—‘You’re not going to believe this, but Luke’s a pastor,’” he said. ‘It created some intrigue, and people started coming. I used to have a note in my phone of how many people came to our church because I went to CrossFit Grandview. It was up to like 60 or 70 before I stopped counting because it was impossible.” Peterson’s good at evangelism, and his church is too—last year, they welcomed around 500 first-time visitors. When he preaches, he knows about half his audience is probably unchurched. Pastor Luke Peterson (right) chats with Capital Church attendees / Courtesy of Capital Church Facebook This is unusual in a country where 40 million adults have stopped attending church over the last 30 years, and where 76 percent of pastors said “fostering connections with unchurched people” is a need in their church. Much has changed since the Billy Graham rallies of the ’60s, the door-knocking of the ’80s, and seeker-sensitive church billboards of the ’90s. In the past, “you could randomly walk up to the person pumping gas next to you and say, ‘Do you know Jesus?’” said Perimeter Church pastor Jeff Norris. “Could that still work? Sure. But more and more, we tell people to invite neighbors into their home. The reality is that evangelism is much slower, and more relational, than it used to be.” Today, people aren’t as likely to read the Bible, think it’s the Word of God, or go to church . But they’re also less hostile to Christianity than they were five years ago. And while they read the Bible less—especially in Gen Z—the trajectory is moving up . “We’re not past ‘my truth, your truth,’” said Rob Warren, pastor of Doxa Church in Madison, Wisconsin. “But people aren’t as sure that their truth is actually true.” These days, evangelistically effective churches are keeping evangelism front of mind in the way they preach, train, and encourage their congregations. They’re celebrating small wins. And they’re leading with a high view of Scripture, prayer, and God’s sovereignty. “We’ve seen all of our ministries grow—from kids to youth to college ministry to Doxa Church as a whole,” Warren said. “It’s not just one demographic of people who are getting saved. God’s doing something.” Times Have Changed Thirty years ago, evangelical churches leaned on programs like Evangelism Explosion or Continuous Witness Training to deliver evangelistic focus and training, church leader Thom Rainer said . Those structured initiatives fit well in a culture that was more Christian and more institutionalized—it took an average of 20 church members to reach one person for Christ per year. Today, it takes 50, Rainer said . “Evangelism efficacy, evangelism effectiveness, has definitely diminished.” That trend is likely to continue. As social media and AI fill our time and increase our social anxiety, even relational evangelism is growing more difficult. As social media and AI fill our time and increase our social anxiety, even relational evangelism is growing more difficult. “I’ve got a new couple that moved into my neighborhood a while ago, and I haven’t even seen them yet,” said Daniel Simmons, executive pastor of campuses and central discipleship at The Summit Church. This means equipping the congregation is more challenging—and important—than ever before. “Evangelism can be this thing that is so burdensome and guilt-driven,” said pastor Christian Gracia. He planted King’s City Church in Las Vegas in 2024 with around 80 people and has seen the church grow to more than 400. “People can feel like they’re not ready or not good enough at evangelism,” Gracia said. “They don’t always know what to say, and can feel like a terrible Christian because they don’t do it. And I always want to help them understand that’s not true.” Start with Leadership If church leaders want to create a culture of evangelism in their church, there’s only one place to start, said Warren, who has baptized 150 people in the last eight months. “Tell me 10 people that you’ve shared the gospel with over the last month or two,” he said. “Because if the leadership team is not doing that, then it’s just an aspirational thing and you’re not going to be able to sustain it. You need those ‘just the other day’ stories.” At Perimeter, they’re putting structure around this. This PCA megachurch in Atlanta was planted by a gifted evangelist, Randy Pope, in 1977. Over the years, they’ve seen thousands come to Christ. Greear, similar conversations are taking place. “We only grew 2 percent this year—we have not grown much over the past few years,” Simmons said. “We did some real soul searching in the spring, and found that our people have lost that invitation culture.” So Summit staff are reminding themselves of their goals. “Every ministry needs to know how they contribute to reaching lost people with the gospel, including the ones that may not intuitively do it,” Simmons said. “We’ve got a strong prayer ministry here.
